topic: DKA in children: ISPAD fluid and insulin protocol

slides.title: Can you crack this PICU emergency?
slides.subtitle: Test your ISPAD 2022 DKA fluid & insulin protocol!

slides.title: Case Clues: 8-yr-old in PICU
slides.subtitle: Spot the severity & first step
points: 25 kg child with **polyuria, vomiting** & Kussmaul breathing
Vitals: HR 142/min, BP 96/60 mmHg, **CRT 2 sec**, drowsy
VBG: **pH 7.08**, HCO3 6 mEq/L, Na 132, K 3.8 mEq/L
RBS **480 mg/dL**, urine ketones 4+, **fruity breath**
slides.highlight: Pause & decide: Severity, initial fluid bolus & when to start insulin?

slides.title: Diagnosis & ISPAD 2022 Cut-offs
slides.subtitle: Did you catch the updated HCO3 threshold?
points: **Severe DKA**: pH <7.1 (here 7.08) or HCO3 <5 mEq/L
ISPAD 2022 DKA cut-off: BG >200 mg/dL + **pH <7.3 or HCO3 <18**
Mild: pH <7.3 or HCO3 <18; **Moderate**: pH <7.2 or HCO3 <10
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: ISPAD 2022 raised the DKA HCO3 cut-off from <15 to <18!

slides.title: Step 1: ISPAD Fluid Resuscitation
slides.subtitle: Fluids BEFORE insulin saves lives
points: No shock here: give **10 mL/kg 0.9% NS** (250 mL) over 30–60 min
If hypotensive shock: **20 mL/kg 0.9% NS** rapid IV bolus
Deficit (~10% for severe) + maintenance over **24–48 hours**
Use **0.45% to 0.9% NS**; do NOT subtract the 10 mL/kg bolus
slides.highlight: Red flag: Rapid excess fluid increases cerebral injury risk!

slides.title: Step 2: Insulin & K+ Timing
slides.subtitle: Never rush insulin in DKA
points: Start regular insulin **1–2 hrs AFTER** starting IV fluids
Dose: **0.05–0.1 U/kg/hr** IV infusion; NO IV bolus
Add **40 mEq/L K+** once urine output is seen & K+ <5.5
If K+ <3.5 mEq/L: give K+ first & **delay insulin** till >3.5
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Never give an IV insulin bolus in pediatric DKA!

slides.title: Step 3: Dextrose & Transition
slides.subtitle: Keep insulin running to clear ketones
points: Add **5% dextrose** when BG hits 250–300 mg/dL (or drops >90/hr)
Keep BG **150–250 mg/dL**; step up to D10–D12.5 if dropping fast
Reduce insulin to **0.05 U/kg/hr** only if BG falls despite D10–12.5
Stop IV insulin when **pH >7.3, HCO3 >15–18** & tolerating oral
slides.highlight: Give rapid-acting SC insulin 15–30 min before stopping IV

slides.title: DKA Traps: Cerebral Injury vs NaHCO3
slides.subtitle: Cerebral Injury || NaHCO3 Rule
points: Signs: Headache, **bradycardia**, altered sensorium || Routine NaHCO3 is **contraindicated**
Rx: **Mannitol 0.5–1 g/kg** IV over 15 min || Increases cerebral injury & hypokalemia
Alt: **3% NaCl 2.5–5 mL/kg** IV over 15 min || Consider only if **pH <6.9** + cardiac failure
Elevate head 30°, reduce fluids by **one-third** || Never correct acidosis with bicarb alone
slides.highlight: Red flag: Treat clinically at bedside—do NOT delay for CT scan!

slides.title: ISPAD 2022 Viva Checklist
slides.subtitle: 4 numbers examiners always ask
points: Diagnostic HCO3 cut-off: **<18 mEq/L** (Severe <5 mEq/L)
Initial bolus (no shock): **10 mL/kg 0.9% NS** over 30–60 min
Insulin infusion: **0.05–0.1 U/kg/hr** after 1–2 hrs of fluids
Cerebral injury: **Mannitol 0.5–1 g/kg** or 3% NaCl 2.5–5 mL/kg
slides.highlight: Exam pearl: Fluids first, check K+ before insulin, dextrose <300!

caption:
Would you start insulin immediately in this 8-year-old? Swipe to test your PICU instincts!

DKA management is a guaranteed MD/DNB viva and OSCE station, and ISPAD 2022 brought critical updates you cannot miss:
• Updated HCO3 diagnostic threshold (<18 mEq/L)
• Exact fluid bolus & deficit replacement rules without overhydration
• Safe insulin timing, potassium replacement & dextrose titration
• Bedside management of cerebral injury

What was the trickiest part of this case for you—the HCO3 cut-off, fluid rate, or K+ timing? Let us know below!

doctor_check: Slide 2: Replaced repeated 'weight 25 kg' in point 4 with 'fruity breath' for better clinical clues.
Slide 4: Updated severe DKA fluid deficit from '7–10%' to '~10% for severe' per ISPAD 2022 (~5% mild, ~7% moderate, ~10% severe).

Slide 6: Changed DKA resolution HCO3 target from '>18' to '>15–18' (ISPAD 2022 uses pH >7.3 and HCO3 >15 mmol/L as hyperchloremic acidosis can delay HCO3 >18) and clarified 'D10–12.5' before reducing insulin.

Slide 7: Replaced late 'Cushing triad' with 'altered sensorium' alongside headache and bradycardia for earlier cerebral injury recognition, and sharpened highlight to warn against delaying treatment for CT scan.
Slide 8 & 9: Refined exam pearl to 'check K+ before insulin' (insulin is only delayed if hypokalemic) and fixed wording repetition in CTA.
